verdict.rationale: The two production refactors are nearly identical and both preserve behavior: same call ordering, same messages, same statuses, and the `_release_stock(order.items)` call in `_charge` is equivalent because every item has been reserved by that point. B's characterization tests are a bit stronger. They check the shipping threshold on both sides (4999 and 5000), check that a declined payment or an out-of-stock order does not redeem the coupon, and assert that no gateway charges or inventory changes happen on early rejection. B's `_discount_cents` also takes only `vip` instead of the whole customer.
a_issues: Does not test that a declined payment leaves the coupon unredeemed, which is a production-relevant side effect
Shipping threshold is only checked at 5000 and above, not just below it
Invalid-coupon test does not assert that the gateway was never charged
b_issues: `test_declined_payment_does_not_redeem_the_coupon` calls `coupons.redeem` inside the test, the same awkward pattern its report criticizes in the existing test
Renamed the validator to the vaguer `_validate`; A's `_validate_items` is clearer

verdict.rationale: Both refactors are nearly identical and preserve behavior: same step order, same error messages and status values, and the duplicated release loops are merged into one helper. Releasing `order.items` on decline is equivalent because every item was reserved by that point. A's tests cover slightly more of the risky production paths: a declined payment does not redeem the coupon, the shipping threshold is checked at both 4999 and 5000, and an invalid quantity leaves the inventory log and charges untouched. B's tests are also correct and add a useful exactly-once redemption check, but they leave the declined-payment coupon path untested.
a_issues: test_out_of_stock_releases_items_reserved_so_far asserts the coupon still returns 10%, but the coupon has 2 uses, so this would pass even if it had been redeemed; the report overstates what that test proves
Does not explicitly test that a successful checkout redeems the coupon exactly once (the existing test only shows it was redeemed at least once)
b_issues: No test that a declined payment leaves the coupon unredeemed, which is a meaningful production path the refactor moved
test_non_positive_quantity_is_rejected does not check that nothing was reserved or charged
Free-shipping boundary is only checked at 5000, not just below it
